correctness.rationale: The prescribed nonnegative coefficients on P_(4j+1), s>1, make an absolutely uniformly convergent positive-definite S2 Schoenberg kernel. Interior Darboux Legendre asymptotics with differentiated remainder reduce the equatorial odd increment to -(A/sqrt(2pi))sum j^(-s-1/2)sin(4jh)+O(h). With alpha=s-1/2 in (1/2,1), a Riemann-sum/Abelian limit yields the nonzero constant 4^alpha Gamma(1-alpha)sin(pi alpha/2)/(sqrt(2pi)alpha). The extra O(j^(-s-delta)) coefficient tail contributes o(|h|^alpha) after splitting at j~1/|h|. This proves the pointwise sharp Hölder exponent, not a full global norm statement; positive semidefiniteness is not strict for only odd degrees. The previous published theorem has exactly the same gamma coefficient after Gamma reflection, verified numerically/symbolically for s=1.2,1.4. Source check.py tests finite Legendre recurrences; it cannot prove infinite asymptotics.
